entries.title: [Comment] The 2025 Wakley–Wu Lien Teh Prize Essay: the profile of future doctors
entries.description: Medicine is in a time of profound transformation: artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the boundaries of diagnosis, treatment, and drug development, rapidly expanding the technological capabilities of health professionals and researchers.1 Yet, health inequity has not improved accordingly and might even be widening across multiple dimensions. Repeated global health crises remind us that pandemics know no borders and that individual wellbeing is more closely intertwined with global and public health than ever.

entries.title: [World Report] Gavi replenishment falls short of US$9 billion target
entries.description: At its sixth replenishment, Gavi fell short of its fundraising target after the USA withdrew all financing and the other key donors reduced their support. Ann Danaiya Usher reports.

entries.title: [Correspondence] AI in clinical trials is missing from CONSORT and SPIRIT 2025 guidelines
entries.description: The CONSORT 20251 update represents a step forward in improving transparency in randomised clinical trial reporting, and the SPIRIT 20252 update similarly aims to enhance completeness in trial protocols. However, one crucial omission that stands out is the absence of any guidance on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in trial design, conduct, or analysis. AI-based tools are increasingly used in clinical research for purposes such as eligibility screening, adaptive randomisation, outcome adjudication, and statistical modelling.

entries.title: [Correspondence] Stereotactic radiotherapy for nAMD: areas for improvement
entries.description: We read with interest the Article by Timothy L Jackson and colleagues1 on the STAR trial for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).1 This study introduces a novel approach to managing nAMD using stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT). Although the findings are promising, several areas warrant further attention.

entries.title: [Articles] Epidemiology and phylogenomic characterisation of two distinct mpox outbreaks in Kinshasa, DR Congo, involving a new subclade Ia lineage: a retrospective, observational study
entries.description: Sustained human-to-human transmission occurred after repeated self-limiting introductions of subclade Ia documented since 2023, which has cocirculated with subclade Ib in Kinshasa from July, 2024. Increased APOBEC3 driven changes in the new subclade Ia lineage support a shift towards human-to-human transmission. These findings reveal important changes in mpox transmission dynamics and suggests that any monkeypox virus subclade has the potential to cause sustained human outbreaks when favourable transmission conditions are met.

entries.title: [Comment] Be brave: women and girls need to remain at the centre of the HIV response
entries.description: 2025 marks a turning point in the HIV response. Experts are suggesting a projected 24% decrease in HIV funding over the next year in the context of reductions to international aid by several governments, extensive cuts to the US Agency for International Development, and withheld funds for the US President's Emergency Fund for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).1 These cuts are likely to lead to an estimated 4·43–10·75 million new HIV infections and 0·77–2·9 million HIV-related deaths in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs) by 2030.

entries.description: Childbirth can be a defining life experience, but it can also be disempowering for many women. The UK Health Secretary, Wes Streeting, has announced the launch of a national investigation into the failings of maternity services, after reports showing a culture of women not being listened to, their pain and concerns dismissed. Unfortunately, this is a global issue, with women frequently experiencing suboptimal care during childbirth. Many women enter labour unprepared for what is coming. entries.title: [Comment] Mpox in DR Congo: a call to action
entries.description: Monkeypox virus was first identified in 1958 in Asian monkeys used for research at a Denmark laboratory and then in 1970 in humans within the Basankusu district of DR Congo. The clinically severe monkeypox virus clade I has been endemic for more than 50 years in DR Congo, whereas the indolent clade II has been limited to west Africa. entries.title: [Correspondence] Reflections on the Lancet Commission on Investing in Health's Global Health 2050 report
entries.description: The Lancet Commission on Investing in Health's Global Health 2050 report1 emphasises halving premature deaths by mid-century through focused health investments. However, for the strategy to succeed, it must address regional and local contexts. Brazil, a country with vast geographical and demographic diversity,2 highlights the need for tailored health initiatives. Substantial regional disparities exist between the northeast and the south and southeast of Brazil, affecting health-care access, socioeconomic conditions, and disease prevalence.

entries.title: [Articles] Collaboration on the optimal timing of anticoagulation after ischaemic stroke and atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and prospective individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (CATALYST)
entries.description: For people with acute ischaemic stroke and atrial fibrillation, early DOAC initiation (within 4 days) reduced the risk of the composite outcome of recurrent ischaemic stroke, symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage, or unclassified stroke within 30 days. These findings support early DOAC initiation in clinical practice.

entries.title: [Articles] Thyroidectomy with or without postoperative radioiodine for patients with low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer in the UK (IoN): a randomised, multicentre, non-inferiority trial
entries.description: The IoN trial shows that ablation (or postoperative radioiodine) can be avoided for patients with pT1, pT2, and N0 or Nx tumours with no adverse features. Many patients with low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer worldwide can safely avoid postoperative radioiodine and its related hospitalisation and side-effects, which in turn results in lower health-care costs.

entries.title: [Comment] Africa's renaissance amid declining overseas health aid
entries.description: Many African countries have long relied on overseas development aid to implement health programmes. Unfortunately, this aid has fostered dependency and fragmentation, often introducing vertical programmes that operate parallel to government plans. The USA, historically the largest provider of such support (which contributes to the maintenance of the USA's soft power in Africa) has taken a sudden and chaotic U-turn, drastically reducing aid and restructuring or dismantling the institutions responsible for its implementation.

entries.description: For weeks on end, I had been waiting for the bad news, obsessively checking my emails for the dreaded message. As a global health researcher funded by the US National Institutes of Health (NIH), my work was a prime target of the new administration. Weeks passed, and as I read about such messages being delivered to colleagues around the country and at my own institution—Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA—I secretly harboured thoughts that the devastation would spare me. My project was the exception.

He reads widely: poetry and novels, philosophy, history, and economics. entries.title: ADB and GCF Partner to Launch Clean Energy Financing Program in India
entries.description: The Green Climate Fund (GCF) has approved $200 million for a new ADB-led program which aims to unlock large-scale public and private investment in high-impact and emerging clean energy sectors in India.

entries.title: ADB Announces $350 Million for Pakistan to Boost the Role of Women in the Economy
entries.description: ADB has approved a loan of $350 million to support access to finance for women in Pakistan. The funding will support the second phase of the Women-Inclusive Finance Sector Development Program, which includes a $300 million policy-based loan and a $50 million financial intermediation loan designed to fund credit facilities and guarantees that support women’s entrepreneurship through improving their access to finance.

entries.title: ADB, CGIAR, and Gates Foundation Partner to Transform Rice Sector, Uplift Millions of Smallholder Farmers in Asia and the Pacific
entries.description: ADB and CGIAR, with support from the Gates Foundation, have launched a new initiative to boost investments in sustainable and low-carbon rice production with the aim of improving the lives of millions of vulnerable smallholder farmers across Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: ADB President Announces $10 Billion Plan for India’s Urban Transformation
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda announced a 5-year initiative aimed at transforming urban infrastructure across India, directing up to $10 billion, including third-party capital, into urban transformation including metro extensions, new regional rapid transit system corridors, and urban infrastructure and services.

entries.title: ADB and AFD Expand Partnership with $6 Billion Cofinancing Target
entries.description: ADB and Agence Française de Développement (AFD) signed an amendment to their Partnership Framework Agreement today, raising their joint cofinancing target to $6 billion for the period 2026–2028 from their previous 3-year target (2023–2025) of $3 billion. The additional cofinancing will support activities in key sectors.

entries.title: ADB Approves $86 Million to Provide Infrastructure, Services for Displaced People from Myanmar and Host Communities in Bangladesh
entries.description: ADB has approved a $58.6 million grant from the Asian Development Fund and a $28.1 million concessional loan to provide basic infrastructure and critical services for displaced people from Myanmar and host communities in Bangladesh.

entries.title: ADB Approves $400 Million for Resilient, Inclusive Development in Bangladesh
entries.description: ADB has approved a $400 million loan to help Bangladesh enhance its resilience against climate impacts, cut emissions in climate-critical sectors, and promote inclusive development.

entries.title: ADB Approves $500 Million to Stabilize, Reform Banking Sector in Bangladesh
entries.description: ADB has approved a $500 million policy-based loan to stabilize and reform the banking sector in Bangladesh by strengthening regulatory supervision, corporate governance, asset quality, and stability.

entries.title: ADB Approves $100 Million for Humanitarian Relief and Community Resilience for the People of Myanmar
entries.description: ADB has approved a $100 million aid package from the Asian Development Fund to deliver integrated humanitarian assistance and build long-term community resilience for the people of Myanmar.

entries.title: ADB Launches New 5-Year Strategy for Economic Transformation in Nepal
entries.description: ADB has unveiled its new Country Partnership Strategy for Nepal for 2025–2029, setting a comprehensive agenda to support the country’s inclusive, resilient, green, and employment-intensive economic growth.

entries.title: ADB Approves $800 Million Program to Boost Pakistan’s Public Finance
entries.description: ADB has approved an $800 million program to strengthen fiscal sustainability and improve public financial management in Pakistan.

entries.title: ADB Launches Second Mongolian Togrog Bond in 2025
entries.description: ADB has priced its second Mongolian togrog (MNT) bond for the year, raising MNT55.8 billion (approximately $15.6 million) to support a dairy project in Mongolia.

entries.title: ADB Approves $109.97 Million Loan to Boost Advanced Skills and Employability in Gujarat
entries.description: ADB has approved a $109.97 million results-based loan to support the Government of Gujarat in advancing its vision of becoming a global industrial hub through a stronger, more future-ready workforce.

entries.title: Public Development Banks Launch Clean Oceans Initiative 2.0
entries.description: Building on a shared commitment to marine sustainability, six public development banks launched the Clean Oceans Initiative 2.0, a renewed and expanded partnership dedicated to drastically reducing plastic pollution in the world’s oceans.

entries.title: ADB President Signals Bigger Singapore Presence in Talks with Prime Minister
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda met Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Singapore today, where he set out plans to double the size of ADB’s Singapore office. He also reaffirmed the bank’s $10 billion pledge to help finance the ASEAN Power Grid and underscored the importance of deeper regional cooperation as Singapore prepares to assume the ASEAN chair in 2027.

entries.title: ADB President Announces Paris Office, Deepens Partnerships at Financing for Development Conference
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda engaged European leaders and key partners during a mission to France and Spain, culminating in the announcement of a new ADB office in Paris.

entries.title: Heads of Multilateral Development Banks Commit to Strong Joint Action on Development Priorities
entries.description: The Heads of Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) have met in Paris, hosted by the Council of Europe Development Bank, which currently chairs the Heads of MDBs Group. The meeting focused on advancing their joint efforts to address development priorities.

entries.title: ADB Supports Resilient Infrastructure Development in Eastern Thailand
entries.description: ADB and the Government of Thailand have signed a $68.74 million loan agreement to provide resilient connectivity infrastructure to the U-Tapao Airport in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC), a manufacturing and innovation hub in eastern Thailand.

entries.title: ADB President Reaffirms Strong Support for Regional Cooperation and Integration at BIMP-EAGA and IMT-GT Summits
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda has reaffirmed ADB’s strong commitment to advancing regional cooperation and integration at the 16th Summits of the Brunei Darussalam–Indonesia–Malaysia–Philippines East ASEAN Growth Area (BIMP-EAGA) and the Indonesia–Malaysia–Thailand Growth Triangle (IMT-GT).

entries.title: Antarctic waters getting saltier as sea ice wanes
entries.description: Using data from ESA’s SMOS satellite, scientists have revealed a surprising shift in the Southern Ocean – surface waters around Antarctica are growing saltier, even as sea ice is diminishing rapidly. This finding defies the norm because melting ice typically freshens ocean surface water. The implications are far-reaching as changes in this remote region can disrupt global ocean currents, affect climate patterns, and alter ecosystems far beyond the Antarctic.

entries.title: Clingy planets can trigger own doom, suspect Cheops and TESS
entries.description: Astronomers using the European Space Agency’s Cheops mission have caught an exoplanet that seems to be triggering flares of radiation from the star it orbits. These tremendous explosions are blasting away the planet’s wispy atmosphere, causing it to shrink every year. This is the first-ever evidence for a ‘planet with a death wish’. Though it was theorised to be possible since the nineties, the flares seen in this research are around 100 times more energetic than expected.

entries.title: Defying physics: This rare crystal cools itself using pure magnetism
entries.description: Deep in Chile’s Atacama Desert, scientists studied a green crystal called atacamite—and discovered it can cool itself dramatically when placed in a magnetic field. Unlike a regular fridge, this effect doesn’t rely on gases or compressors. Instead, it’s tied to the crystal’s unusual inner structure, where tiny magnetic forces get tangled in a kind of “frustration.” When those tangled forces are disrupted by magnetism, the crystal suddenly drops in temperature. It’s a strange, natural trick that could someday help us build greener, more efficient ways to cool things.

entries.title: Can one vanishing particle shatter string theory — and explain dark matter?
entries.description: Scientists are on the trail of a mysterious five-particle structure that could challenge one of the biggest theories in physics: string theory. This rare particle—never seen before and predicted not to exist within string theory—might leave behind vanishing tracks in the Large Hadron Collider, like ghostly footprints that suddenly disappear. Spotting it wouldn’t just shake up physics theory—it might also reveal clues to dark matter, the invisible stuff that makes up most of the universe.
